_transcription: PAGE MAP: the booklet is 16 rendered pages (idx 0-15 = printed folios 1-16), every one accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB5/5, SET No. 3, Q.P. Code 57/5/3, BIOLOGY (Theory), 2 hours, 35 marks, 15 printed pages, 13 questions). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 (folios 3-15). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. The tops of all seven odd indices open in Hindi (idx 1 Hindi instructions and Q1-2, idx 3 Hindi Q3-4, idx 5 Hindi Q5-6, idx 7 Hindi Section B / Q7-12, idx 9 Hindi Section C / Q13(a), idx 11 Hindi Q13(b) passage, idx 13 Hindi Q13(b) sub-parts), so no English overflow onto an odd page and no parity inversion. idx 14 is English (Q13(b)(i)-(iii)); idx 15 (folio 16) is blank. The paper is born-digital; every row was read off the full-size page and the English text layer was diffed against the vision read: they agree on every English line, and the text layer carries none of the figure labels, which were read off the page. Decimals: the paper prints ORDINARY full stops ('2.5 mg/kg'), left as printed. Structure as printed: Section A Q1-6 @2, Section B Q7-12 @3, Section C Q13 case-based @5 = 35. Instruction (iv) says internal choices exist but gives no count; the roster was built from the scheme's bare ORs (text layer: three, all bare lines) and each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper: Q2, Q5 and Q13 (three alternatives). Section B has no internal choice on this set. The '//' inside the scheme's Q10 answer is an alternative FORM of the answer (a PCR diagram), not an internal choice. Q8 and Q12 print (a) and (b) with no OR between them, so each is one row. FOLLOWER of 57/5/1 (and sibling of 57/5/2): 14 of the 18 rows are questions already in 57/5/1 or 57/5/2, each confirmed on this paper's own page (and against its text layer) and given the sibling's stem and context byte for byte (57/5/1 Q3a/b = Q2a/b, Q4 = Q3, Q1 = Q4, Q6a/b = Q5a/b, Q12 = Q8, Q7 = Q9, Q9 = Q10, Q11 = Q12, Q13ai-iii and Q13b = Q13ai-iii and Q13b). New on this set: Q1 (Glomus mycorrhiza), Q6 (population density of fishes in a river, a re-authored version of 57/5/2's bacterial-culture Q6 with a different organism and answer), Q7 (allergens, IgE and mast cells) and Q11 (a non-viral, non-vector method of gene transfer into plant cells). The four drawings that are also in the siblings (the S.T.P. flow diagrams, the four solar-radiation graphs, the pBR322 map and the RNAi bar graph) were read on this paper's pages; the _figure notes describe this PDF and the page indices are this PDF's. The scheme prints the same void note on Q5(b)(i) as 57/5/1 does on its Q6(b)(i). Quotes straight as printed; scientific names plain (Glomus prints bold italic, Cynomolgus bold, Meloidogyne incognitia bold italic). Typos kept as printed: Q1 'mycorrhizial' and 'Elaborate how is this association', Q2(a) 'cocain', Q6 'total population density of the number of fishes in river', Q13(a) passage 'Cloning of genes, play' and 'one such engineered vectors', Q13(b) passage 'An experiment was carried to study', Q13(b)(i) 'brings an effect', Q13(b)(iii) 'incognitia'. One question asks the student to draw (Q13(a)(iii) the EcoRI fragments), so one _drawFigure. No question examines content the rationalised NCERT book removed, so no _outOfSyllabus.

questions.stem: Many members of genus Glomus form a mycorrhizial association with plants. Elaborate how is this association beneficial to the plants.
State the mode of action of cocain on human body. Write the scientific name of the source plant it is obtained from.
Enumerate four most common warning signs of drug and alcohol abuse amongst the youth.

Study the given diagram of Sewage Treatment Plant (S.T.P.) and answer the questions that follow :
S.T.P. (Sewage Treatment Plant) (A): Municipal Sewage \(\rightarrow\) (W) BIOLOGICAL TREATMENT \(\rightarrow\) (X) SEDIMENTATION AND FILTRATION \(\rightarrow\) River
S.T.P. (Sewage Treatment Plant) (B): Municipal Sewage \(\rightarrow\) (Y) SEQUENTIAL FILTRATION \(\rightarrow\) (Z) BIOLOGICAL TREATMENT \(\rightarrow\) River
(a) Which one of the two 'S.T.P.' (A) or (B) will be more effective in treating the human excreta in the municipal waste?
(b) Write the steps followed in carrying the treatment of the sewage in step (Z), once the BOD of sewage is reduced significantly till it is passed on to the "anaerobic sludge digesters".
questions._figure: DECORATIVE: two flow diagrams, each a drawn building labelled Municipal Sewage feeding two boxes in sequence and then a drawn river; every box label, its letter (W, X, Y, Z) and the order of the boxes are carried as text in the stem, so the drawing adds nothing. Page idx 4.

questions.stem: Ringworm is one of the most common infectious fungal disease in humans. Name any two genera of fungi which cause ringworm and state any of its two symptoms.

(i) Write the observations made at the end of Connell's field experiment on barnacles on the rocky sea coasts of Scotland.
(ii) Name any two categories of organisms that in general are adversely affected by competition.

questions.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
questions.stem:
The graphs (X) and (Y) given below depict the diurnal variations in the solar radiations in the month of June (Summer) and in December (Winters) :
(i) Which of the two graphs depicts tropical region and temperate regions respectively ?
(ii) Which of the two regions (X) or (Y) will show high biological diversity and why?
questions._figure: REQUIRED: four small graphs side by side, each of Solar radiation (y, arrow upward) against Time of the day (x, ticks 1 hr., 12, 24 hr.), each with one hump-shaped curve peaking at 12; the first two are captioned June 22 and Dec. 22 under the label (X), the last two June 22 and Dec. 22 under the label (Y). How tall each hump is, and so how much each region's radiation changes between June and December, is what part (i) asks the student to read, so it is withheld here. Page idx 6.
questions._cbseVoided: Note: Since graphs shown are not conclusive enough for drawing any interpretation, so one mark to be given to students, if attempted.
questions._flag: The void covers part (i) only (1 of the 2 marks); part (ii) is marked normally.

questions.stem: What would be the best method to measure the total population density of the number of fishes in river and why ?

Many people experience allergic symptoms of sneezing or wheezing on exposure to certain substances in the environment. Give two examples of such substances. Which type of antibodies are produced by the body in response to these substances ? Mention the role of mast cells in this kind of allergic response.

(a) Enlist two criteria that are used to identify a region for maximum protection as 'Biodiversity hotspots'.
(b) Name any two "hotspot" regions in our country.
'An HIV patient normally doesn't die of 'AIDS', but death is caused due to many other infections.' Do you agree with the statement ? Give explanatory reasons in support of your answer.

questions.subtopic: Isolation, Cutting and Amplification of DNA
questions.stem: A cell free method of amplifying DNA first developed in the mid 1980's revolutionized the field of biotechnology. Name the method and explain the basic steps of the technique involved.
Non viral and non vector methods are sometimes used to transfer genes or alien DNA into a plant cell. Explain one such method used in genetic engineering.

(a) How does a gene therapy involving direct modification of the cells, in order to achieve a therapeutic goal is used in the treatment of ADA deficiency ? Explain.
(b) A host cell must be made competent, before it is able to receive an rDNA. Justify.
questions._flag: Part (b) (1 of the 3 marks) is on making the host competent, which is Biotechnology: Principles and Processes / Cloning Vectors and Competent Host; the row is filed on the 2-mark gene-therapy part (a).

questions.context: Cloning of genes, play a very significant role in genetic engineering, helping the transfer of desirable foreign genes into different hosts. The scientists, to make this process easier and effective are creating engineered vectors in such a way that they help easy linking of foreign DNA and selection of recombinants from non recombinants. 'pBR322' is one such engineered vectors developed by scientists. A diagram of an engineered vector pBR322 is given below :
questions.stem: Name the host for this cloning vector.

questions.context:
RNA interference (RNAi) holds great potential as a therapeutic agent for the treatment of human diseases and as biocontrol agents in controlling pests in the field of agriculture. An experiment was carried to study the use of 'RNAi' for the potential treatment of disorders of cholesterol metabolism. Some people possess genetic mutations with elevated levels of ApoB gene which predisposes them to coronary artery diseases.

Lowering the amount of ApoB can reduce the number of lipoproteins and lower the blood cholesterol.

Tracy Zimmerman and her colleagues used RNAi in 2006 to reduce the level of ApoB in non human primates Cynomolgus monkeys.

One group of monkeys were given RNAi treatment (small interfering RNAs, SiRNAs) (doses 1 mg/kg SiRNAs), second group of monkeys were given RNAi treatment (doses 2.5 mg/kg SiRNAs) and third group of monkeys were injected with saline.

The results of the study are depicted in the graph below :
questions.stem:
(i) How does the treatment with 2.5 mg/kg brings an effect on cholesterol metabolism when compared from 24 hours and 144 hours.
(ii) Write any two natural sources from where dsRNA molecule could be obtained for silencing the specific mRNA.
(iii) How is RNAi used in controlling the infection on the roots of tobacco plants by the nematode Meloidogyne incognitia.
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a bar graph of Relative serum cholesterol (% predose) (y, 0 to 120 in steps of 20) against Time (hours) at 24, 48, 144 and 264 (x), with three bars at each time keyed Saline - X (diagonal hatching), 1 mg/kg - Y (dotted outline) and 2.5 mg/kg - Z (solid grey). The bar heights, and so how the 2.5 mg/kg bar changes between 24 and 144 hours, are what part (i) asks the student to read, so they are withheld here. Page idx 12.
